title: PDF Compression Lossy vs Lossless — Technical Breakdown & Comparison
metaDescription: Understand lossy vs lossless PDF compression algorithms. Learn how Flate/Deflate stream encoding and JPEG image downsampling shrink PDF file size safely.
author: Zcompressor Engineering
heroHeadline: PDF compression: lossy vs. lossless algorithms.
heroDescription: A technical breakdown of how PDF stream encoding, Flate/Deflate algorithms, and lossy image DCT downsampling work together to reduce document file sizes.

sections.heading: Lossless PDF stream compression (Flate / Deflate).
body: Lossless compression reduces file size by reorganizing structural metadata, stripping duplicate font subsets, and applying Flate/Deflate zlib encoding to raw content streams.

Because lossless compression is 100% reversible, 0% visual quality is lost. However, lossless compression alone usually achieves only 10% to 25% size reduction if the PDF contains heavy scanned images.

sections.heading: Lossy image stream optimization (DCT & Downsampling).
body: To achieve 70% to 90% size reductions (e.g. shrinking a 3 MB document under 200 KB), lossy image compression is required for embedded photo and scan streams.
Zcompressor intelligently separates vector text elements (which remain 100% lossless) from background raster graphics (which undergo smart bicubic resampling and JPEG DCT quantization).

faq.q: Does Zcompressor use lossy or lossless compression?
faq.a: Zcompressor uses a hybrid model: 100% lossless compression for vector text, fonts, and layout structures, combined with smart lossy downsampling for heavy embedded images.
